title: Chief executives, senior officials and legislators
outlook_rationale: Employment is likely to grow moderately as Cyprus’s professional services, finance, shipping, technology and tourism sectors expand, alongside continued demand for senior public-sector leadership. AI will support analysis and administration more than replace executive accountability, though the limited number of leadership posts and slower growth in some sectors temper the outlook.
exposure_rationale: AI can substantially assist with analysis, briefing, communications, planning and routine decision support, making senior leaders more productive and potentially changing staffing needs. However, the role still depends heavily on accountable judgment, negotiation, political or organisational relationships, and leadership in real-world settings, which limits direct automation.

title: Administrative and commercial managers
outlook_rationale: Administrative and commercial managers should see modest demand from Cyprus’s tourism, financial, shipping, and professional-services sectors, as well as its growing role as a technology and business hub. AI may reduce demand for some administrative functions, while the group’s historical employment decline tempers the growth outlook; managerial, strategic, and client-facing responsibilities are less readily automated.
exposure_rationale: Administrative and commercial managers spend substantial time on digital work such as planning, reporting, analysis, communications, and coordinating business processes, where AI can automate tasks and increase the productivity of teams. Their roles also depend on leadership, negotiation, accountability, and context-sensitive decisions, which limits full automation but is likely to reshape how the work is done.

title: Production and specialised services managers
outlook_rationale: Demand should grow moderately as Cyprus expands construction, professional services, healthcare, education, and digitally enabled sectors, increasing the need for managers to coordinate specialised operations. AI may automate some planning and administrative tasks, but is more likely to augment managerial work than replace it; the unusually high historical growth rate is unlikely to persist unchanged over the next decade.
exposure_rationale: AI can substantially assist with planning, forecasting, reporting, and resource allocation, making managers more productive and potentially reducing some administrative workload. However, this broad group includes roles overseeing physical production and specialised services that require on-site judgment, staff coordination, and accountability, limiting direct automation.

title: Hospitality, retail and other services managers
outlook_rationale: Tourism and hospitality remain important growth drivers in Cyprus, supporting demand for managers, while retail and other services should see steadier expansion. Digital tools and automation may reduce some routine management tasks, but are more likely to reshape roles than eliminate them; the group’s strong historical growth is unlikely to continue at the same pace.
exposure_rationale: AI can substantially assist with forecasting, pricing, scheduling, inventory, reporting, and customer communications, making managers more productive and potentially reducing administrative staffing needs. However, hospitality and retail managers still coordinate on-site operations, handle staff and customer issues, and make context-dependent decisions in physical workplaces, limiting automation of the core role.

title: Science and engineering professionals
outlook_rationale: Demand should grow as the green and digital transitions increase the need for engineering and scientific expertise, with Cyprus’s construction, energy, technology, and professional-services sectors providing additional support. AI is likely to automate some routine analytical tasks but mostly complement specialist work; the strong historical growth rate supports a positive outlook, though it is unlikely to continue unchanged for a decade.
exposure_rationale: Many core tasks—modelling, analysis, research synthesis, technical documentation, and design—are digital and increasingly AI-assisted, potentially raising productivity and reducing demand for some routine analytical work. However, experiments, fieldwork, site inspections, physical prototyping, and safety-critical engineering judgment still require human expertise and presence, so exposure varies substantially across the group.

title: Health professionals
outlook_rationale: Ageing populations, rising chronic-disease needs, and persistent healthcare staffing shortages are likely to support strong demand for health professionals across Cyprus and the EU. AI may improve diagnostic and administrative efficiency, but is more likely to augment than replace clinical work; workforce and funding constraints temper the pace of growth.
exposure_rationale: AI can significantly assist health professionals with documentation, image interpretation, clinical decision support, and treatment planning, potentially increasing productivity and changing workflows. However, much of the work involves physical examination, procedures, and direct patient interaction that require human presence and judgment, limiting automation of core duties.

title: Teaching professionals
outlook_rationale: Employment is likely to grow moderately as migration, private and international education, and demand for specialized teaching support offset demographic pressures that may limit growth in some school-age cohorts. AI is more likely to assist teachers than replace them, while public-sector hiring and workforce replacement will sustain demand.
exposure_rationale: AI can substantially assist teaching professionals with lesson preparation, learning materials, routine assessment, feedback, and administrative tasks, potentially increasing productivity and changing staffing needs. However, teaching still depends heavily on in-person interaction, classroom management, adapting to learners, and professional judgment, which limits direct automation.

title: Business and administration professionals
outlook_rationale: Demand should continue to grow as Cyprus’s financial, shipping, professional-services and technology sectors expand and face increasing regulatory and digital-transformation needs. AI will automate some routine analysis and administrative tasks, tempering growth, but is more likely to augment many professional roles than eliminate them.
exposure_rationale: Most business and administration professionals do knowledge work using digital information, so AI can automate or accelerate substantial tasks such as analysis, reporting, document preparation, and forecasting. Human judgment, accountability, regulatory requirements, and client or stakeholder relationships remain important, but are unlikely to prevent major restructuring across these roles.

title: Information and communications technology professionals
outlook_rationale: Demand should remain strong as Cyprus develops its technology, fintech, financial-services and shipping sectors, while EU digitalisation and cybersecurity needs support hiring. AI may automate some routine ICT tasks, but it is also likely to increase demand for professionals who build, integrate and secure digital systems; the exceptional historical growth rate is unlikely to persist unchanged.
exposure_rationale: ICT professionals do most of their core work digitally, including software development, systems analysis, database design, testing, and technical documentation—areas where AI is advancing rapidly and can automate or accelerate substantial tasks. Human expertise remains important for architecture, security, complex requirements, and accountability, but AI-driven productivity is likely to significantly reshape staffing and workflows across Cyprus and the EU.

title: Legal, social and cultural professionals
outlook_rationale: Employment is likely to grow moderately, supported by demand for legal and professional services, social support, and cultural activity in Cyprus and the EU. AI will automate some research, translation, and routine content work, tempering growth, while demographic needs and Cyprus’s expanding professional-services sector provide support.
exposure_rationale: Much of the work involves digital research, writing, analysis, documentation, and communication, where AI can automate tasks and substantially increase productivity—especially in legal and policy-related roles. However, the group also includes occupations requiring human judgment, trust, direct social interaction, or creative and cultural work, which limits how much of the core job can be automated.

title: Science and engineering associate professionals
outlook_rationale: Demand should grow as Cyprus and the EU invest in construction, infrastructure, renewable energy, and digital transformation, while the group’s recent employment growth provides a positive baseline. Automation may streamline routine technical tasks, but is more likely to complement these workers than eliminate demand for hands-on technical support.
exposure_rationale: AI can significantly assist with technical documentation, data analysis, design support, and monitoring, especially in engineering and laboratory roles. However, many duties involve operating or calibrating equipment, conducting tests and inspections, and responding to physical-world conditions, which limits automation across this diverse group.

title: Health associate professionals
outlook_rationale: Ageing populations in Cyprus and across the EU will increase demand for diagnostic, therapeutic and other health support services, while Cyprus’s expanding healthcare sector adds to hiring needs. AI may automate some routine tasks but is more likely to complement these roles than replace them; the historical growth trend supports a strong, though not exceptional, outlook.
exposure_rationale: Health associate professionals may use AI for documentation, triage support, image or laboratory analysis, and treatment planning, making parts of their information-processing work more efficient. However, many core duties involve hands-on procedures, patient care, and real-time interaction that require physical presence and human judgment, limiting direct automation.

title: Business and administration associate professionals
outlook_rationale: Demand should grow moderately as Cyprus’s financial, professional, tourism, and technology-related sectors expand, supporting roles in finance, sales, business services, and compliance. AI and workflow automation will reduce some routine administrative tasks, tempering growth, while digital transformation and regulatory needs sustain demand across the group.
exposure_rationale: Much of the group’s work involves processing information, preparing documents, analysing data, coordinating transactions, and communicating digitally—tasks where AI can automate substantial work or increase worker productivity. Client-facing duties, negotiation, regulatory judgment, and local context provide some resilience, but are unlikely to prevent major restructuring across the group.

title: Legal, social, cultural and related associate professionals
outlook_rationale: Demand for social and community services should rise with ageing populations and continued public-sector and migration-related needs, while Cyprus’s tourism and cultural sectors support related roles. AI may automate some routine legal and administrative tasks, tempering growth, but is less likely to replace the group’s interpersonal and service-oriented work.
exposure_rationale: AI can substantially assist with research, drafting, documentation, and routine administrative work across this group, particularly in legal support and cultural-content tasks. However, many roles depend on direct human interaction, practical activities, performance, or contextual judgment, limiting automation of their core work.

title: Information and communications technicians
outlook_rationale: Demand for ICT infrastructure, cybersecurity, cloud services, and digital transformation should support strong growth in Cyprus and across the EU, reinforced by Cyprus’s ambitions as a technology and fintech hub. AI may automate some routine support tasks, but expanding systems and networks will sustain demand for technicians who install, maintain, and troubleshoot them.
exposure_rationale: AI can substantially automate or accelerate routine help-desk responses, monitoring, documentation, and basic network or system diagnostics, reducing time needed for many information-processing tasks. However, the group also includes hands-on installation, equipment maintenance, and contextual troubleshooting that often require physical presence and human interaction, limiting overall exposure.

title: General and keyboard clerks
outlook_rationale: AI, digital self-service, and workflow automation are likely to reduce demand for routine clerical and keyboard tasks across the EU. Cyprus’s public sector and growing professional, financial, and tourism services should cushion the decline, but are unlikely to fully offset it.
exposure_rationale: Most duties involve digital, routine information processing—such as entering data, preparing documents, maintaining records, and handling correspondence—where AI and workflow automation can both perform tasks and reduce staffing needs. Some roles include coordination or in-person service that still requires human judgment, but this is unlikely to offset the substantial potential for restructuring.

title: Customer services clerks
outlook_rationale: Digital self-service, chatbots, and AI-enabled customer support are likely to reduce demand for routine clerical customer-service work, consistent with the group’s historical employment decline. Growth in Cyprus tourism, financial services, and other customer-facing sectors will partly offset these losses, while roles requiring complex or in-person assistance are less readily automated.
exposure_rationale: Much of the work involves handling inquiries, processing requests, and updating records through digital systems—tasks increasingly supported or automated by chatbots, voice AI, and customer-service software. Human judgment and empathy remain important for complex or sensitive cases, and some roles involve in-person contact, but AI is likely to substantially reshape staffing and daily workflows.

title: Numerical and material recording clerks
outlook_rationale: Employment is likely to decline as accounting, data entry, inventory tracking, and routine record-keeping are increasingly automated or integrated into digital business systems. Continued activity in Cyprus’s tourism, construction, and logistics sectors should sustain some demand, limiting the decline rather than eliminating these roles.
exposure_rationale: Most core duties—entering and checking figures, maintaining stock or production records, processing documents, and updating databases—are routine information-processing tasks that AI and automated systems can increasingly handle. Some roles still involve physical stock checks or coordination with workers and suppliers, but these tasks are a limited barrier to substantial automation and productivity gains.

title: Other clerical support workers
outlook_rationale: Digitisation, self-service systems, and AI-enabled document processing are likely to reduce demand for several clerical support roles across Cyprus and the EU. E-commerce and ongoing postal needs may partly offset these losses, but are unlikely to reverse the overall gradual decline.
exposure_rationale: Many duties in this group involve routine information processing—such as filing, coding, proofreading, personnel records and copying—that AI and digital systems can automate or speed up substantially. Mail handling and other in-person or physical tasks are less directly exposed, so the group’s overall exposure is below that of fully digital clerical occupations.

title: Personal service workers
outlook_rationale: Employment is likely to grow as Cyprus’s tourism and hospitality sectors expand and demand for in-person services remains resilient across the EU. Self-service technology and automation may limit growth in some routine tasks, but they are unlikely to replace the interpersonal and practical work central to this group.
exposure_rationale: Personal service workers typically provide hands-on services and interact directly with customers in settings such as restaurants, hotels, salons, and tourist attractions. AI may help with bookings, translation, recommendations, and routine administration, but the core work generally requires physical presence, practical skill, and real-time human interaction.

title: Sales workers
outlook_rationale: Employment is likely to decline moderately as e-commerce, self-service checkout, and AI-enabled sales tools reduce demand for some in-person retail roles, consistent with the group’s recent historical decline. Tourism and hospitality, in-person customer service, and Cyprus’s expanding business sectors should cushion losses, so a steep contraction is unlikely.
exposure_rationale: AI can automate or streamline product recommendations, routine customer enquiries, transaction processing, and some sales administration, while digital tools may let fewer workers handle more sales activity. However, many sales workers in Cyprus and the EU serve customers in person, demonstrate products, handle goods, and respond to unpredictable needs, limiting automation of the core work.

title: Personal care workers
outlook_rationale: Ageing populations in Cyprus and across the EU will increase demand for home, residential, and other personal care, while automation is unlikely to replace the hands-on and interpersonal aspects of the work. Labour shortages and public funding constraints may temper growth, but demographic demand supports a strong positive outlook.
exposure_rationale: Personal care workers rely on hands-on assistance, physical presence, and real-time human interaction, which are difficult for AI to replace. AI may help with care documentation, scheduling, or monitoring, but these are peripheral to the core work.

title: Protective services workers
outlook_rationale: Employment is likely to remain broadly stable, with modest support from tourism, public safety needs, and demand for security at commercial sites and events. AI-enabled surveillance may limit growth in routine guarding, but it is unlikely to replace most frontline protective roles; public-sector staffing and demographic pressures provide some offset.
exposure_rationale: Protective services work is primarily performed in person and often involves physical intervention, unpredictable situations, and real-time judgment, which limits direct automation. AI may assist with surveillance, dispatch, risk assessment, and report writing, but these are supporting tasks rather than the core duties.

title: Market-oriented skilled agricultural workers
outlook_rationale: Employment is likely to continue declining as farm consolidation, mechanisation and productivity improvements reduce demand for skilled workers; the historical employment CAGR of -1.4% points to a similar downward trend. Ageing farm populations and limited appeal to younger workers reinforce the decline, although Cyprus’s agricultural niches and migrant labour may moderate it somewhat.
exposure_rationale: The core work involves hands-on crop or livestock production, operating equipment, and responding to changing physical conditions, which limits direct AI automation. AI may assist with planning, monitoring, and farm records, but these are supporting tasks and are unlikely to displace the need for workers in the field.

title: Market-oriented skilled forestry, fishery and hunting workers
outlook_rationale: Employment is likely to edge down as mechanisation and consolidation limit labour needs in forestry and capture fisheries, while Cyprus has a relatively small traditional forestry and fishing workforce. Sustainable forest management and expanding aquaculture provide some offsetting demand, but are unlikely to outweigh those pressures across this broad occupation group.
exposure_rationale: The core work is physical and takes place outdoors or aboard vessels, involving hands-on forestry, fishing, or hunting tasks in variable environments. AI may assist with planning, monitoring, navigation, and paperwork, but is unlikely to automate much of the work itself.

title: Building and related trades workers, excluding electricians
outlook_rationale: Employment is likely to grow moderately as Cyprus’s construction and real-estate activity, infrastructure investment, and building renovation support demand for skilled trades. Automation is limited for much on-site work, while ageing workers and labor shortages may constrain growth; the historical employment trend supports a positive but not exceptional outlook.
exposure_rationale: The core work involves hands-on construction, repair, and finishing in changing physical environments, requiring manual skill and on-site judgment that AI cannot readily replace. AI may assist with plans, measurements, scheduling, and documentation, but these are peripheral to the work and are unlikely to greatly reduce the need for workers.

title: Metal, machinery and related trades workers
outlook_rationale: Demand for metal and machinery trades workers should remain supported by construction, shipping, equipment maintenance, and investment in renewable energy and infrastructure. Automation may limit growth in some routine production tasks, but skilled maintenance and repair work is less readily replaced, while retirements and skills shortages provide further support.
exposure_rationale: The core work involves hands-on fabrication, machining, installation, and repair in physical environments, where variable conditions and skilled manual tasks limit direct AI automation. AI may assist with diagnostics, planning, and automated machinery, but these tools are more likely to change workflows than replace most workers.

title: Handicraft and printing workers
outlook_rationale: Employment is likely to continue declining as digital media reduces demand for printing and automation limits labour needs in related production trades; the group’s historical employment decline reinforces this outlook. Tourism and demand for locally made crafts may support some artisanal work in Cyprus, but are unlikely to offset the broader structural contraction.
exposure_rationale: Most work involves hands-on craft production, operating or tending printing equipment, and handling physical materials, which limits direct AI substitution. AI can still reshape digital design, prepress, job planning, and routine production workflows, making exposure meaningful but uneven across the group.

title: Electrical and electronic trades workers
outlook_rationale: Demand for electrical and electronic trades workers should grow moderately as Cyprus and the EU expand construction, renewable energy, building efficiency, EV charging, and grid upgrades. Hands-on installation and maintenance are difficult to automate, though productivity gains and weaker demand for some traditional electronics repair work may temper growth.
exposure_rationale: The core work involves installing, maintaining, and repairing electrical or electronic equipment in physical environments, requiring hands-on skill, safety judgment, and often on-site presence. AI can assist with diagnostics, technical documentation, and work planning, but is unlikely to replace much of the practical work in the near term.

title: Food processing, wood working, garment and other craft and related trades workers
outlook_rationale: Employment is likely to remain broadly stable: Cyprus’s tourism and food sectors and ongoing construction activity support demand for food-processing and woodworking trades. Automation, productivity gains, and competition from imported or lower-cost garments and crafts will limit growth, while many hands-on and specialised tasks remain difficult to automate fully.
exposure_rationale: Most work involves hands-on processing, machine operation, finishing, or craft skills in physical workplaces, which limits direct automation by AI. AI may improve production planning, pattern design, quality inspection, and machine control, but these tools are more likely to support workers than replace the core manual tasks.

title: Stationary plant and machine operators
outlook_rationale: Employment is likely to remain broadly stable, with modest support from investment in utilities, water treatment, energy infrastructure, and construction-related production. Automation and process-control technologies will limit hiring growth, while Cyprus’s relatively small industrial base constrains expansion; the group’s strong historical growth is therefore unlikely to continue at the same pace.
exposure_rationale: The work is anchored in operating and monitoring physical plant, responding to equipment conditions, and following safety procedures, so it cannot be done entirely on a computer. AI can improve process control, fault detection, and predictive maintenance, potentially reducing staffing needs, but workers remain important for on-site oversight and intervention.

title: Assemblers
outlook_rationale: Assembler employment is likely to decline moderately as automation, robotics, and offshoring reduce demand for routine production-line work across the EU. Cyprus has a relatively small manufacturing base, and while renewable-energy and technology-related production may create some roles, these gains are unlikely to offset the broader trend.
exposure_rationale: Assemblers mainly perform hands-on work with parts, tools, and machinery in physical production settings, which limits the direct impact of software-based AI. AI-enabled robotics and inspection systems may automate or support repetitive, standardized assembly tasks, but deployment depends on the production process and does not remove the need for physical operations and oversight.

title: Drivers and mobile plant operators
outlook_rationale: Demand from tourism, freight and logistics, public transport, and Cyprus’s construction sector should support moderate employment growth, with driver shortages and gradual demographic growth adding pressure. Automation and the shift to electric vehicles will change the work but are unlikely to eliminate many roles within a decade; autonomous vehicle adoption and efficiency gains may nevertheless temper growth.
exposure_rationale: The core work involves physically operating vehicles or mobile machinery in changing real-world conditions, where safety, practical judgment, and human presence limit near-term automation. AI can improve routing, monitoring, and scheduling, while autonomous systems may reshape some roles over time, but adoption is constrained by infrastructure, regulation, and the diversity of operating environments.

title: Cleaners and helpers
outlook_rationale: Employment is likely to grow modestly as Cyprus’s tourism and hospitality sectors, commercial services, and an ageing population sustain demand for cleaning and household support. Automation is limited for many hands-on tasks, though labour shortages, cost pressures, and some mechanisation may constrain growth; migration will remain important to staffing.
exposure_rationale: The core work involves physical cleaning in varied homes, offices, hotels, and other settings, requiring on-site presence and hands-on effort. AI may assist with scheduling or coordination, while cleaning robots could automate some repetitive tasks, but these are limited substitutes for the broader duties of cleaners and helpers.

title: Agricultural, forestry and fishery labourers
outlook_rationale: Employment is likely to decline as mechanisation, farm consolidation and productivity gains reduce demand for routine agricultural and fishery labour; the group’s historical employment trend is already negative. Seasonal labour needs and worker shortages in Cyprus may cushion the decline, but are unlikely to reverse it over the next decade.
exposure_rationale: The core work is physical and typically performed outdoors or in other hands-on settings, such as planting, harvesting, tending animals, and maintaining forests or fishing operations. AI may assist indirectly through planning, monitoring, or machinery, but it is unlikely to replace much of the labourers’ on-site manual work in the near term.

title: Labourers in mining, construction, manufacturing and transport
outlook_rationale: Automation, mechanisation and productivity improvements are likely to reduce demand for routine manufacturing, transport and materials-handling labour, continuing the group’s historical decline. Construction activity in Cyprus and ongoing labour needs in logistics will partly offset this, while worker shortages and migration may sustain employment levels.
exposure_rationale: The core work is physical and location-bound, involving carrying, loading, cleaning, and assisting with construction, manufacturing, or transport tasks that require human presence and handling in changing environments. AI may affect scheduling and coordination, while robotics and automated equipment could reduce demand for some routine tasks over time, but these are indirect or uneven effects rather than widespread automation of the group’s core work.

title: Food preparation assistants
outlook_rationale: Tourism growth and steady demand from hotels, restaurants, and food services in Cyprus are likely to support hiring, while similar demand across the EU provides a positive baseline. Kitchen automation and labour-saving preparation methods will temper growth, and the exceptionally strong historical employment rate is unlikely to continue over the next decade.
exposure_rationale: Food preparation assistants mainly perform hands-on tasks such as washing, peeling, portioning, and assembling food in busy kitchens. AI may assist with ordering or scheduling, but the core work requires physical presence and dexterity, and kitchen automation is limited.

title: Street and related sales and service workers
outlook_rationale: Employment is likely to decline modestly as online retail, formal retail channels, and changing consumer habits reduce demand for some street-vending work; AI is a limited direct factor. Cyprus tourism and visitor spending should sustain demand for street-based sales and services, offsetting some of that pressure.
exposure_rationale: The work is mainly performed in person and involves selling or providing services in public settings, often with hands-on tasks and real-time customer interaction. AI may assist with payments, stock management, or promotion, but these are peripheral to the core work.

title: Refuse workers and other elementary workers
outlook_rationale: Employment is likely to decline moderately as automation, digital services, and more efficient waste-management operations reduce demand for some elementary tasks; the group’s historical employment trend also points downward. Municipal sanitation, tourism-related cleaning, and ongoing population growth in Cyprus should sustain demand for essential services and temper the decline.
exposure_rationale: The work is primarily physical and takes place in real-world settings, involving tasks such as collecting refuse, street cleaning, and other manual duties that require human presence. AI may assist with route planning, scheduling, or monitoring, but these are peripheral to the core work and automation faces practical challenges in varied environments.
